answer.evidence: The main body is a wide wooden cart box. Rows 7-15 are a band of horizontal plank stripes, and the vertical posts at rows 5-6 cross it. The band ends at a lighter strip at rows 16-17, which acts as the front-edge line and eave shadow. Below it, rows 18-26 form a front face with vertical panels and a dark opening, which is 9 rows. The wheel on the right and the small pile at the bottom left (rows 27-31) are side details and decor. The top band could also be read as a vertical plank face, so the top-surface reading is only moderately certain. The drawing is a single intact cart rather than scattered debris, though an overturned cart is plausibly debris.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden overturned cart with a wheel and a small pile of goods. Its outline leans dark brown rather than neutral black (1% near-neutral dark edge pixels), which matches the Beodeul approach. The wood shows plank lines and some grain, but it is built from only about 4 lightness steps against 5-6 in the references. It has 7 visible tones per tile, below the stall (17) and well (20) and close to the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 17%, higher than the well and hedge (0%) and the stall (13%), which fits the large flat body panels visible by eye. The wheel and the goods pile are simple, with little per-plank highlight and little dot texture. It is competent but thinner and flatter than the best same-kind references such as the stall and well, so I fail it when in doubt.
